newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Opposition warns of potential violence in rallies.
newsitem.headline: Opposition warns of potential violence in rallies.

text.p: A leader of Serbia's pro-democracy movement said on Thursday there was no guarantee that demonstrators in the streets would remain peaceful in face of a new police crackdown.

Vuk Draskovic, a leader of the Zajedno (Together) coalition, told Reuters Television that President Slobodan Milosevic was plotting with shadowy paramilitary groups to crush opposition supporters who have demonstrated in their hundreds of thousands for six straight weeks in an attempt to reverse the ruling party's election fraud.

A ban on street marches imposed after a December 24 Belgrade riot between opposition activists and government loyalists, the first violence since the rallies began, led to sporadic police assaults on protesters.

Draskovic said Zajedno's principle of non-violence remained intact but, if police threats worsened, "nobody can give guarantees people would not reply in a way of self-defence to protect their lives and human dignity.
"Unfortunately this could be the beginning of bloodshed and civil war," he said as many thousands of Zajedno supporters massed in central Belgrade for the 46th consecutive day.
